cards.etymology: bound「set limits / 设界」的过去分词作形容词
cards.gloss_en: limited by a clear constraint (time, scope, resources)
cards.gloss_zh: 有界的；被明确限制住的
cards.avoid: *have limit spike*；*limited time research* 乱套；别把「有时限」拼成 *have time bound*
cards.home_scene: Research spike ticket keeps growing. You mark the investigation as **time-bounded** — two days, then a write-up — and state the work is **bounded by** the auth path only, not the whole billing surface.
cards.cloze: Research spike ticket keeps growing. You mark the investigation as ______ — two days, then a write-up — and state the work is ______ the auth path only, not the whole billing surface.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（spike 工单）：「这个调研有时间限制，只能做两天，而且范围只限 auth。」→ 用 time-bounded / bounded by … 改写成职场英文。
cards.rewrite_answer: Mark this spike as time-bounded — two days, then a write-up. The work is bounded by the auth path only, not the whole billing surface.
cards.pitfalls: *bounded by X* = 上限是 X；别写成 *bound of X*；*time-bounded* 比 *has a time limit* 更像工单/spike 用语

cards.etymology: 拉丁 distinguere「separate / 区分」→ distinction
cards.gloss_en: a clear difference that matters for meaning or policy
cards.target_chunks: `make a distinction between A and B`; `a key distinction`
cards.use: *make a distinction between A and B*; *a key distinction*; *draw a distinction*
cards.avoid: *make difference between*；*a big different*；别把「区分」拼成 *do distinction*
cards.home_scene: Marketing/support copy blurs beta and GA entitlements. You force the room to **make a distinction between** beta limits **and** GA rights so support doesn’t overpromise. **A key distinction**: beta users get early access, not SLA-backed uptime.
cards.cloze: Marketing/support copy blurs beta and GA entitlements. You force the room to ______ beta limits ______ GA rights so support doesn’t overpromise. ______: beta users get early access, not SLA-backed uptime.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句：「我们要分清楚 beta 限制和 GA 权利，这是一个关键差别。」→ 用 make a distinction between / a key distinction 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: We need to make a distinction between beta limits and GA rights. A key distinction: beta users get early access, not SLA-backed uptime.
cards.pitfalls: 固定说 *make/draw a distinction between A and B*，不要 *make difference between*；与 *nuance*（细微差别）相比，*distinction* 更强调「必须划清的界限」

cards.etymology: 拉丁 durare「to last / 持久」→ durable
cards.gloss_en: lasting; built to remain reliable over time (fix or storage)
cards.gloss_zh: 持久的；经得起时间的（修复/存储）
cards.avoid: *long-time fix*；*strong storage*；别把「持久修复」拼成 *forever patch*
cards.home_scene: Architecture review of a flaky queue fix. Someone proposes another temporary patch. You push for **a durable fix**, not another band-aid, and argue we should also pick **durable storage** so the queue state survives restarts.
cards.cloze: Architecture review of a flaky queue fix. Someone proposes another temporary patch. You push for ______, not another band-aid, and argue we should also pick ______ so the queue state survives restarts.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（架构评审）：「不要再临时补丁了，我们要一个能长久的修复，还有能持久的存储。」→ 用 a durable fix / durable storage 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Push for a durable fix, not another band-aid. We should also pick durable storage so queue state survives restarts.
cards.pitfalls: *durable* ≠ 只是 *strong*；强调「经得起时间」，不是力气大；别用 *forever patch* / *long-time fix* 替代 *a durable fix*

cards.etymology: 拉丁 facere「做」→ 古法 faisible「可做的」→ 英 feasible
cards.gloss_zh: 可行的；资源约束下能落地的
cards.use: *more feasible under/within …*; *not feasible under …*; *a feasible option/timeline*
cards.avoid: *feasible to do* 乱套；别把「可行」拼成 *can do*
cards.home_scene: Daily standup. A teammate pushes a full big-bang launch next Friday to “get it over with.” You look at headcount and the open Sev-2 queue: a phased rollout is **more feasible under** our current bandwidth, and a single cutover is **not feasible under** that constraint. You propose 10% → 50% → 100% with a kill switch, and ask PM to confirm stakeholder messaging before anyone commits Friday.
cards.cloze: Daily standup. A teammate pushes a full big-bang launch next Friday. You look at headcount and the open Sev-2 queue: a phased rollout is ______ our current bandwidth, and a single cutover is ______ that constraint.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 弱句：「这周五一次全上线不太行，人不够，还是分批吧。」→ 用 more feasible under/within … 或 not feasible under …。
cards.rewrite_answer: A phased rollout is more feasible under our current bandwidth; a full cutover is not feasible under that constraint.
cards.pitfalls: 名词是 *feasibility*，不是 *feasibleness*；评估句式优先 *whether X is feasible*，少用中式 *X is can*
cards.why_this_chunk: more/not feasible under … binds practicality to constraints; stronger than bare possible/can do; viable is longer-term.

cards.etymology: 体育/航空复合词 hand + off；职场引申为交接
cards.gloss_en: transfer of responsibility, context, and next actions to the next person
cards.gloss_zh: （值班/班次）交接；责任与上下文移交
cards.avoid: *hand over notes* 乱套为唯一说法；别把「干净交接」拼成 *clean give*
cards.home_scene: End of on-call day shift. Before you leave Slack, you write **handoff notes** the night person must read: open pages, mitigations tried, and who to page. Goal is a **clean handoff** — no tribal knowledge stuck in your head.
cards.cloze: End of on-call day shift. Before you leave Slack, you write ______ the night person must read: open pages, mitigations tried, and who to page. Goal is a ______ — no tribal knowledge stuck in your head.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（值班结束）：「下班前写交接笔记，要做到干净交接。」→ 用 handoff notes / clean handoff 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Before you leave, write handoff notes the night person must read. Goal is a clean handoff — no tribal knowledge stuck in your head.
cards.pitfalls: 名词常 *handoff*（连写）；动词常 *hand off*；*clean handoff* = 上下文齐全、对方能接着干；不是「礼貌地说再见」

cards.etymology: 拉丁 inspicere「look into / 察看」→ inspect
cards.gloss_en: look carefully at evidence (logs, traces, diffs) before changing code
cards.gloss_zh: 仔细检查；审看（日志/链路等）
cards.use: *inspect the logs*; *inspect … for …*; *inspect traces*; *inspect the diff*
cards.avoid: *check carefully the logs* 语序别扭；别把「排查」一律写成 *look look*
cards.home_scene: Pager for a p99 latency spike. Before changing code, you **inspect the logs** and traces and **inspect** the hot path **for** a lock or N+1 query. Fix comes after evidence, not after a guess.
cards.cloze: Pager for a p99 latency spike. Before changing code, you ______ and traces and ______ the hot path ______ a lock or N+1 query. Fix comes after evidence, not after a guess.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（p99 告警）：「改代码前先仔细看日志，再查热路径有没有锁或 N+1。」→ 用 inspect the logs / inspect … for … 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Before changing code, inspect the logs and traces, and inspect the hot path for a lock or N+1 query.
cards.pitfalls: *inspect X for Y* = 在 X 里找 Y；别只说 *check check*；比 *look at* 更强调「有目的地审看证据」

cards.etymology: 拉丁 iter「旅程」→ itinerarium「旅行记录/路线」→ itinerary
cards.gloss_zh: 行程安排（拜访路线+时间）
cards.target_chunks: `draft/confirm/lock the itinerary`; `any change to the … itinerary`
cards.use: *draft/confirm/lock the itinerary*; *any change to the … itinerary*
cards.avoid: 用 *itinerary* 当 *agenda*；别堆 *travel schedule plan*
cards.home_scene: Email: please **draft/confirm** **the itinerary** for next week’s onsite; **any change to the** VIP **itinerary** must clear security before we **lock the itinerary**. Ops won’t book cars until the itinerary is locked.
cards.cloze: Email: please ______ for next week’s onsite; ______ must clear security before we ______. Ops won’t book cars until the itinerary is locked.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（onsite 邮件）：「请起草确认下周行程；任何行程改动要过安保，然后锁定行程。」→ 用 draft/confirm/lock the itinerary 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Please draft and confirm the itinerary for next week’s onsite; any change to the VIP itinerary must clear security before we lock the itinerary.
cards.pitfalls: 用 *itinerary* 当 *agenda*；别堆 *travel schedule plan*

cards.etymology: 拉丁 magnus「great / 大」+ facere「make / 使」→ magnify
cards.gloss_en: make something larger in impact or appearance; enlarge the blast radius of a risk
cards.use: *magnify the risk*; *magnify … into …*; *magnify the blast radius*
cards.avoid: *make risk bigger* 当唯一说法；别把「放大风险」拼成 *big the risk*
cards.home_scene: Risk review before launch. A tiny edge-case bug looks minor in isolation, but on a hot path it would **magnify the risk**. Left alone, it could **magnify** a single timeout **into** a full-region outage.
cards.cloze: Risk review before launch. A tiny edge-case bug looks minor in isolation, but on a hot path it would ______. Left alone, it could ______ a single timeout ______ a full-region outage.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（上线风险评审）：「这个小 bug 在热路径会把风险放大，一次超时可能放大成全区故障。」→ 用 magnify the risk / magnify … into … 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: On a hot path that edge-case would magnify the risk. Left alone, it could magnify a single timeout into a full-region outage.
cards.pitfalls: *magnify A into B* = 把 A 放大成 B；别写成 *magnify A to become B* 冗长版当唯一块；职场风险语境优先 *magnify the risk*，不是字面「用放大镜看」

cards.etymology: 法语 nuance「色调深浅」← nue「云」→ 细微差别
cards.gloss_en: a subtle difference in meaning, tone, or feeling
cards.gloss_zh: 细微差别；措辞的微妙处
cards.target_chunks: `a nuance between A and B`; `with one nuance: …`
cards.use: *a nuance between A and B*; *with one nuance: …*; *capture/miss a nuance*
cards.home_scene: FAQ review: the draft misses **a nuance between** “recommend” **and** “require.” I agree on the conclusion, **with one nuance:** timing still needs Legal.
cards.cloze: FAQ review: the draft misses ______ “recommend” and “require.” I agree on the conclusion, ______: timing still needs Legal.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（FAQ 评审）：「草稿漏了 recommend 和 require 之间的细微差别；结论我同意，但有一个 nuance：时机还要过 Legal。」→ 用目标语块改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: The draft misses a nuance between “recommend” and “require.” I agree on the conclusion, with one nuance: timing still needs Legal.

cards.etymology: 拉丁 recipe「拿取」（药方命令式）→ 食谱/配方
cards.gloss_en: repeatable steps that produce a result; also cooking instructions
cards.use: *step-by-step recipe*; *a recipe for success/failure*; *no single recipe for …*
cards.home_scene: PR on the runbook: keep this as a **step-by-step recipe** on-call can repeat. Vague ownership + tight deadlines is **a recipe for** failure.
cards.cloze: PR on the runbook: keep this as a ______ on-call can repeat. Vague ownership + tight deadlines is ______ failure.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（runbook PR）：「把 runbook 写成值班能照着重复的逐步配方；权责不清+截止日期紧就是事故配方。」→ 用 step-by-step recipe / a recipe for … 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Keep this as a step-by-step recipe on-call can repeat. Vague ownership plus tight deadlines is a recipe for an incident.

cards.pronunciation_tip: ri-KUR-ing；重音在 KUR，双写 r 不改变读音
cards.etymology: 拉丁 recurrere「run back / 跑回」→ recurring
cards.gloss_en: happening repeatedly on a schedule or pattern
cards.use: *a recurring meeting*; *set … as recurring*; *a recurring issue*; *recurring revenue*（财务侧）
cards.avoid: *repeat meeting*；*again and again meeting*；别把「周会」拼成 *every-week meeting* 当正式写法
cards.home_scene: Scheduling the eng sync. Boss asks if this is one-off or every week. You say we should book **a recurring meeting**, not a one-off invite each Monday. In the same thread someone notes the flaky deploy alert is a **recurring issue**, so the sync needs a standing agenda slot.
cards.cloze: Scheduling the eng sync. Boss asks if this is one-off or every week. You say we should book ______, not a one-off invite each Monday. In the same thread someone notes the flaky deploy alert is a ______, so the sync needs a standing agenda slot.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（约会）：「别每周单独发邀请，订一个周期性会议；那个 flaky alert 也是 recurring issue。」→ 用 a recurring meeting / recurring issue 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Book a recurring meeting, not a one-off invite each Monday. The flaky deploy alert is a recurring issue, so give it a standing agenda slot.
cards.pitfalls: 日历语境优先 *a recurring meeting*；财务另有 *recurring revenue*，别在同一句里硬混；别写 *repeat meeting* / *again meeting*

cards.etymology: 拉丁 retinere「hold back / 留住」→ retention
cards.gloss_en: the act of keeping users, customers, or employees over time
cards.gloss_zh: 留存；把用户/客户/员工留住的程度
cards.avoid: *keep rate*；*retain rate*；别把「用户留存」拼成 *user keep*；勿与 *data retention policy*（数据保留策略）混用
cards.article: (no hit in this post’s article body)
cards.home_scene: Monthly growth review. Churn rose last month, and the PM asks what actually keeps paying users. You put **user retention** on the slide first, then walk the room through the **retention rate** by cohort so we debate the product policy, not vanity signups.
cards.cloze: Monthly growth review. Churn rose last month, and the PM asks what actually keeps paying users. You put ______ on the slide first, then walk the room through the ______ by cohort so we debate the product policy, not vanity signups.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（增长会）：「先把用户留存放到 slide，再按 cohort 看留存率。」→ 用 user retention / retention rate 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Put user retention on the slide first, then walk through the retention rate by cohort so we debate product policy, not vanity signups.
cards.pitfalls: 别和 *data retention policy*（合规里的数据保留期限）混淆；growth 语境优先说 *user retention* / *retention rate*；避免中式 *keep rate* / *user keep*

cards.etymology: 现代复合词 roll + out（产品发布义约 mid-20c）
cards.gloss_en: a planned release of a feature or change, often in stages
cards.gloss_zh: （功能/变更的）上线推送；发布节奏
cards.use: *phased rollout*; *rollout plan*; *gradual rollout*; *roll out to N%*
cards.avoid: *roll out plan* 当名词时漏连写；别把「分批上线」拼成 *batch online*；勿与单次 *cutover* 混为一谈
cards.home_scene: Launch doc review for a new feature. You refuse a single cutover and define percent gates by region. The **rollout plan** calls for a **phased rollout**: 5% → 25% → 100%, with kill switches at each gate.
cards.cloze: Launch doc review for a new feature. You refuse a single cutover and define percent gates by region. The ______ calls for a ______: 5% → 25% → 100%, with kill switches at each gate.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（launch doc）：「拒绝一次切全量；rollout plan 要分阶段：5%→25%→100%。」→ 用 rollout plan / phased rollout 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: The rollout plan calls for a phased rollout: 5% → 25% → 100%, with kill switches at each gate.
cards.pitfalls: 名词常用 *rollout*（连写）；动词常 *roll out*；*phased rollout* ≠ 一次 *big-bang cutover*

cards.etymology: 拉丁 spectare「to look / 看」→ spectacle
cards.gloss_en: a dramatic public show — often unhelpful when you need calm incident response
cards.gloss_zh: 场面；公开闹大的「戏」；哗众取宠的公开表现
cards.target_chunks: `make a spectacle of …`; `avoid a public spectacle`
cards.use: *make a spectacle of …*; *avoid a public spectacle*; *turn … into a spectacle*
cards.avoid: *make a show of outage* 乱套；别把「别闹大」拼成 *don’t big show*
cards.home_scene: Incident war room. Someone wants a dramatic public post mid-outage. You warn: don’t **make a spectacle of** the outage while customers are still down — **avoid a public spectacle** until we have a clear status and a fix ETA.
cards.cloze: Incident war room. Someone wants a dramatic public post mid-outage. You warn: don’t ______ the outage while customers are still down — ______ until we have a clear status and a fix ETA.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（故障 war room）：「客户还挂着的时候别把故障闹成公开大场面。」→ 用 make a spectacle of / avoid a public spectacle 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Don’t make a spectacle of the outage while customers are still down — avoid a public spectacle until we have a clear status and a fix ETA.
cards.pitfalls: 职场里常是否定用法：*avoid a public spectacle* / *don’t make a spectacle of X*；别和中性 *visibility* / *transparency* 混为一谈——透明不等于演戏

cards.etymology: 中古英语 stale「不新鲜」；职场引申为过期/未刷新的数据或分支
cards.gloss_en: no longer fresh or up to date (data, cache, branch, approval)
cards.gloss_zh: 陈旧的；未刷新的（数据/缓存/分支）
cards.avoid: *old data* 当唯一说法；别把「过期分支」拼成 *expired branch*（更常说 stale）
cards.home_scene: PR review. CI is green but the branch is 40 commits behind main, so reviewers risk approving **stale data** in the preview. You ask for a rebase: this is **a stale branch** — refresh before we merge.
cards.cloze: PR review. CI is green but the branch is 40 commits behind main, so reviewers risk approving ______ in the preview. You ask for a rebase: this is ______ — refresh before we merge.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（PR 评审）：「分支落后 40 个 commit，预览里可能是过期数据；这是个 stale branch，先 rebase。」→ 用 stale data / a stale branch 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Reviewers risk approving stale data in the preview. This is a stale branch — rebase and refresh before we merge.
cards.pitfalls: *old data* 当唯一说法；别把「过期分支」拼成 *expired branch*（更常说 stale）

cards.etymology: 古英 steoran「掌舵、引导船只」→ 引申为引导方向
cards.gloss_en: guide the direction; course-correct a discussion
cards.gloss_zh: 引导、把讨论/项目拉回正轨
cards.use: *steer … back to …*; *steer … toward/away from*; *steer clear of …*
cards.avoid: 自造 *pull the topic return*；别字面「开方向盘」
cards.home_scene: Design/planning review. The thread slides into button padding and a competitor’s marketing site. You interrupt once: “Can we **steer** this **back to** the decision criteria we wrote on the doc?” Two minutes later someone starts rumor-chat about headcount; you add, “Please **steer clear of** gossip — we still need an owner for the acceptance checks.” The room returns to the checklist.
cards.cloze: Design/planning review drifts into pixels and competitor gossip. You: can we ______ this ______ the decision criteria? And please ______ gossip — we still need an owner for the acceptance checks.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 弱句：「别扯皮了，回到决策标准，竞品八卦别聊。」→ 用 steer … back to … 和/或 steer clear of …。
cards.rewrite_answer: Can we steer the discussion back to the decision criteria? And please steer clear of competitor gossip.
cards.pitfalls: *steer clear of* 是短语，别拆成字面方向盘；*steering committee* = 指导委员会；过去式 *steered*，不是 *stear*
cards.why_this_chunk: steer … back to … = course-correct; steer clear of … = deliberately avoid; not bare guide/drive/avoid talk.

cards.etymology: 拉丁 super「above」+ sedere「sit」→ supersede「坐到上面取代」→ 过去分词 superseded
cards.gloss_en: replaced by something newer or better; no longer the current authority
cards.gloss_zh: 已被取代的；不再作为现行标准的
cards.use: *superseded by …*; *this doc/API is superseded*; *supersede the old …*
cards.avoid: *replaced already by* 堆砌；别拼 *superceded*（常见错拼少一个 s）
cards.home_scene: API docs review. The sidebar still links to the v1 design note as if it were current. You comment: **this doc is superseded** — point readers to v2. The v1 note was **superseded by** the GA contract and must move under Archive.
cards.cloze: API docs review. The sidebar still links to the v1 design note as if it were current. You comment: ______ — point readers to v2. The v1 note was ______ the GA contract and must move under Archive.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（API 文档）：「这篇 v1 设计说明已经不是现行标准了，被 GA 合同取代了。」→ 用 this doc is superseded / superseded by … 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: This doc is superseded — point readers to v2. The v1 note was superseded by the GA contract and must move under Archive.
cards.pitfalls: *replaced already by* 堆砌；别拼 *superceded*（常见错拼少一个 s）

cards.etymology: 拉丁 supplere「fill up / 补足」→ supplemental
cards.gloss_en: extra material that supports the main point but is not the core decision
cards.gloss_zh: 补充的；附带的（非核心决策部分）
cards.avoid: *add materials* 当标签；别把「补充材料」拼成 *extra stuff section* 当正式 RFC 用语
cards.home_scene: RFC review. Extra benchmarks and screenshots are useful but must not bury the decision. You move them under **supplemental materials** and add **a supplemental note** that they inform the choice but are not the decision itself.
cards.cloze: RFC review. Extra benchmarks and screenshots are useful but must not bury the decision. You move them under ______ and add ______ that they inform the choice but are not the decision itself.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 中式弱句（RFC）：「额外基准和截图别淹没决策，放到补充材料，并加一条补充说明。」→ 用 supplemental materials / a supplemental note 改写。
cards.rewrite_answer: Move the benchmarks under supplemental materials and add a supplemental note that they inform the choice but are not the decision itself.
cards.pitfalls: *supplemental* = 额外、非核心；别当成 *essential* / *core*；RFC 里用 *supplemental materials* 比 *extra stuff* 更干净

cards.etymology: 拉丁 tentare/temptare「尝试、试探」→ 中世拉丁 tentativus → tentative
cards.gloss_en: not final; provisional; subject to change
cards.avoid: 日历里用 *busy* 表示「暂定」；别混 *attentive*
cards.home_scene: Wednesday Q3 roadmap sync. Your boss wants a hard launch date for the deck. Legal still has not signed off, so a firm commit would be dishonest. You say you can only share **a tentative timeline** for planning, and you ask the EA to **mark** the follow-up invite **as tentative** until Legal clears. In Slack afterward you write: “Dates are directional — please treat them as changeable.”
cards.cloze: Wednesday Q3 roadmap sync. Your boss wants a hard launch date for the deck. Legal still has not signed off. You say you can only share ______ for planning, and you ask the EA to ______ the follow-up invite ______ until Legal clears.
cards.rewrite_prompt: 弱句：「上线时间还没定死，先随便写个日期，日历先占上。」→ 用 a tentative timeline / mark … as tentative 写可发英文。
cards.rewrite_answer: I can only offer a tentative timeline, not a hard commit. Please mark the invite as tentative until Legal signs off.
cards.pitfalls: 错拼少见，但副词别漏：*tentatively*；日历 *tentative* ≈ 待定接受，≠ *busy*；名词感表达优先用 chunk，不要只丢光杆 *tentative*
cards.why_this_chunk: a tentative timeline = changeable schedule (not merely possible); mark … as tentative = calendar state (not busy).
